findings.statement: 'replacing both sides by least-squares affine fits gives 0.939, a nonlinear gain of 0.0012, so the interactions shape the predicted risk levels far more than the ranking of rows'
findings.check: linearise scope (as_unit entries); refit additive and main-effects models on the 24000 training rows
findings.evidence: the affine fits are in the 32 first-layer ReLU features (the leaves' entries), not in the inputs, so this test keeps the first layer's non-linearity and interactions and measures only the second layer. In the inputs, a main-effects logistic model reaches AUC 0.886 and an additive spline model (non-linear main effects, no interactions) 0.899 (test 0.899), against the model's 0.940; adding pairwise terms gives 0.931. Interactions are worth about 0.04 AUC of ranking, so the conclusion that they shape levels far more than ranking does not hold; 0.0012 is only the second layer's non-linear gain

high_side_core.why: A mixture of five live units that rises with age (mostly above about 60), with bmi in older people, with visits and with score; the bmi-by-age reading is confirmed, but it is not the main carrier of the age effect below 60.

low_side_core.why: Its protective reading (strongest for young people, women, high income with low score, fading with age) is confirmed by probes and subgroups, but six units together carry most of every input's effect, so it is the whole risk-lowering side rather than one mechanism.

unit36_visits_bmi_smoker.why: Off for most people under 60 (acts on 25%), on for older, frequent-visit, heavy or uninsured-smoking profiles, adding risk; confirmed on 747 of 749 older frequent visitors and by the bmi-by-age probe.

unit38_score_urban.why: The rural high-score effect is real (0.84 vs 0.00 at score 95) but the unit is also age-gated and 73% of its active rows are not high-score rural.

unit42_age_female.why: Lowers risk for young people, about three times as much for young women as young men, and fades with age, sooner for men; confirmed by probes and subgroups.

unit47_income.why: Lowers risk most for high income with a low score, but it acts on 62% of all rows, including older high earners at average scores.
